I'm working on some lean proofs for economics, and my agents came up with some physics math as a side effect. I am not a physicist, are these results interesting?

  • The Inverted Bekenstein Bound: The formalization proves that, counter to standard area-law intuition, a boundary provably does not bound the bulk in these specific generalized contexts.

  • Negative Lovelock: It proves that Lovelock's theorem (which states that the Einstein tensor is the only divergence-free symmetric rank-2 tensor constructed from the metric) fails outside a commutative sub-class. Commutativity itself is what draws the boundary of whether the uniqueness is forced.

  • Krein Dissipation: A strict proof that Krein theory (indefinite-signature stability) cannot exist on the dissipative hemisphere.
